title: Real homework from public tables: invented-only students fall below the rule on real tables, and real homework lifts them there
request: Phase 7 (the owner): a student behind every choice; 29.15 gives three points a real-table set from OpenML's own declarations, beside the invented one, with its own sealed partition, and scores each student on both.
plan: Read each profiled OpenML table once more to build its columns' states exactly as the invented sets build theirs, with DCLab's rule answers.
Truths from each dataset's declarations, through one library function; each table in the lake's own split.
Score the rule, the student and a student trained with real homework on both dev sets, beside the commonest label.

decisions.decision: Read the data files again rather than use the lake's cached states.
decisions.why: The cache has no rule answers and no outcome's value count, and the task state needs it; the owner said yes to the OpenML download for the lake.

decisions.decision: Each table in the lake's split, not the sets' own hash.
decisions.why: The lake's gold and the decisions export already file each OpenML table under the lake's split: one table must sit in one split everywhere.

decisions.decision: Identifier truths only from datasets that declare a row identifier.
decisions.why: Most OpenML keys are left as features, undeclared: labelling them not identifiers would mark the rule wrong where it is right.

decisions.decision: The semantic role stands in for target.column as the third point.
decisions.why: target.column has no invented set and no student to score on both.

decisions.decision: The students with real homework are not adopted.
decisions.why: They are measured on dev rows only; a sealed exam on the real partitions is the owner's call.

change: dclab_core/declared.py (0.87.0); dclab_rnd/real_homework.py (fetch, derive, build, score, the GLiNER answers matched by input); decisions/real_v1 (its manifest committed, rows and sealed files rebuilt by the command); models_real_v1 cards; evidence/campaigns/real_homework_v1/RHW-001; the register's real scores beside the rule's and the commonest label's; the archive keeps the real sets.

findings.defect: Students trained on invented tables fall below the rule on real ones.
findings.scenario: Real dev: the task student 0.748 against the rule's 0.971; the role student 0.803 against 0.822, near the commonest label's 0.783.
findings.cause: Invented outcomes and columns do not cover how real tables look.
findings.fix: A student trained with real homework too: 0.981 and 0.996 on real dev, 0.008 and 0.013 below on invented dev; reported, not adopted.

findings.defect: The real identifier set was nearly one class and partly wrongly labelled.
findings.scenario: 29 identifiers in 26,350 columns: always answering no scored 0.998 on dev, above the rule.
findings.cause: Every dataset's columns were labelled, though most datasets declare no identifier.
findings.fix: Only datasets that declare one; every score beside the commonest label's, with recall.

findings.defect: The real and invented label definitions differ, unsaid.
findings.scenario: A declared-numeric code is numeric, an entity key not an identifier, a few whole values regression; a string outcome counted as a disagreement.
findings.cause: The limits named only the uploader's word.
findings.fix: Each difference in the limits; a reason of its own for an outcome whose type names no task.

findings.defect: The lake's gold and the real sets give one table different truths.
findings.scenario: The lake calls every numeric outcome regression and labels every dataset's columns.
findings.cause: The lake's OpenML samples keep 26.2's first reading.
findings.fix: Said in the module, the integration guide and the plan; aligning the lake left for later.

findings.defect: GLiNER's answers were matched by sample id only.
findings.scenario: Columns whose state differs from the lake's would count an answer to another input.
findings.fix: Matched by the input's fingerprint too.

findings.defect: The committed cards and manifests said wrong things.
findings.scenario: A card said it trained on generated tables only; the per-point policy said 20% sealed.
findings.fix: The card's limits and the manifest's policy say what was done.

findings.defect: The limits understated what GLiNER did not answer.
findings.scenario: A fixed count of 66 differing states, while 853 role decisions had no matching answer.
findings.fix: Coverage beside each score (answered of); the differing states counted in the set's manifest.

measurements.name: RHW-001, the three points on both dev sets
measurements.gate: none: the Done when asks for the scores
measurements.result: real dev: task rule 0.971, student 0.748, with real homework 0.981; role rule 0.822, student 0.803, with real homework 0.996; identifiers rule 1.0, student 0.989, with real homework 0.992 (commonest 0.983); real dev holds 6 identifier tables
limits: Dev rows only; the real sealed partitions unread.
The role's real truths follow the stored type.

outcome: Three points have real-table sets beside the invented ones and every student is scored on both: invented homework alone does not carry to real tables, and the students with real homework wait for a sealed exam.
lessons: Score every answerer beside the commonest label: a set with a rare class makes any accuracy look good.
A real dataset's declarations are a convention: check how often they follow a column's storage before reading a high score as skill.
risks: RHW-001 keeps the limit text written before the review's last fix (a fixed count of differing states).
